reading.source_scope_note: Turkish-language explicit word-norming survey,finalN274,of40 preselected mental-capacity concepts. Participants choose Agency/Experience and High/Low after definitions/examples. PAM clusters aggregate category and level counts; TF-IDF quadgram coding summarizes self-explanations. No robot presentation,IAT reaction-time test,unconscious-bias measure,AI performance test or observed social interaction is conducted.
access_limits: All supplied text,tables and sole substantive figure read. ACM public HTML returned403; OpenMETU metadata/full-PDF link checked. No additional appendix,data,code or preregistration identified/obtained.

English candidate pool was translated and filtered for Turkish length/overlap; full original80-item pool and Turkish presentation/material packet are not supplied. No multilingual measurement-invariance or independent test–retest validation performed here.
Clustering and lexical-topic results use published summaries; no raw responses,exact distance/preprocessing settings,full quadgram frequencies or code available for independent reproduction.

Original Greenwald/Nosek/Malle/Weisman and other cited works are not independently fully read. Reference44 journal metadata/abstract consulted for identity only. Norming-paper credit must not become independent credit for all sources it cites.

study.participants: 463survey attempts,280complete submissions,six excluded for not having Turkish as a native language,final274:163female,109male,two nonbinary;ages18–65,mean33.86,SD12.17;263Turkish-only native,11Turkish among native languages. Volunteer online recruitment,not a representative population sample. Anonymous-link274/QR6 describes280completers,not necessarily identities of the six excluded.
study.item_selection: Initial80candidate concepts split26HighAgency,22LowAgency,17HighExperience,15LowExperience. Seven native speakers with cognitive-science backgrounds andC1English translated;two had professional localization experience. Excluded cross-loading,near-synonym,longer-than-three-word and context-heavy moral/philosophical items. Final40preassigned evenly to four target cells; this filtering narrows what structural conclusions can follow.
study.procedure: Each word receives two deliberate binary choices:Agency versusExperience,thenHigh versusLow capacity needed. Category definitions and examples given beforehand;word order randomized but left/right answer positions fixed. Participants take time;no response-time measure. Planning and fatigue examples convey intended level distinctions,not actual cross-species cognitive standards.
study.clustering: 40aggregate item points use Agency count and High count;Experience/Low are their complements. Silhouette favorsk2;authors deliberately also requestk3/4/5 to explore desired finer stimulus groups. k2medoids:self-control andphysicalpain. Similarity clustering combines category andlevel axes,so cluster membership need not equal the majority category of each word.
study.rating_examples: Emotion recognition106Agency/168Experience and empathy113/161 nevertheless sit in firstk2cluster;see178Agency/96Experience sits in second. These are not automatic clustering errors because High/Low coordinates also contribute. The fixed binary response menu and selected item pool do not discover universally exhaustive dimensions.
study.higher_k: k3splits broad experience/physiological groups;k4adds imagine,emotionrecognition,empathy;k5splits experience further. These descriptive requested solutions are not independent replications,validated latent mental modules or a uniquely optimal four-factor result.
study.text_analysis: 257of274answer open questions,valid texts254/251/252/251 after filler removal. TF-IDF examines ngrams,top50quadgrams per four prompts coded by two purpose-blind raters after topic discussion. Three themes:concept/process,agent type,cognitive/physical requirements. Reportedκ.914–.972,overall.945,concerns200selectedquadgrams,not200participants or predictive validity.
study.interpretation: Reported healthy-human/species/complexity language is respondents’ stated conceptualization under supplied instructions,not a normative hierarchy of people,proof of actual human exclusivity,or evidence that lower-rated people have less dignity. Frequency/TF-IDF and rater agreement do not isolate unconscious mental processes or establish that instructions removed every confound.
study.count_boundary: 274×40=10960item-evaluation pairs,each containing two choices;repeated judgments do not increase independent participantN. This is the274-person prior norming source cited in PDF216,now independently fully reviewed as its own publication,not another274-person replication.

summary: No new record. Add original Turkish lexical norming evidence to mind,agency and experience attribution,with explicit task and structural limits. Retain ToM/implicit-bias distinctions as boundaries. Correct two majority-level table labels,arXiv-scheme artifacts and a broken reference with verified author order/locator. Do not inflate40stimulus words into40new behaviors or describe this as an implicit robot-response experiment.

findings.definition: Ascribing or denying mental capacities to another entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing attribution construct; add original lexical norming and stimulus-design limits rather than convert every capacity word or research instrument into another behavior.

evidence.quote: mental capacity attributions, not the states

findings.evidence_scope: The paper explicitly distinguishes capacity attribution from current mental states and norms40Turkish words for future tasks.274volunteers classify words after instruction;aggregate count clustering supports stimulus selection,not a test of actual robot mentality.
findings.boundary: Capacity words,attributed capacities,accurate mentalizing and actual mental states differ. Norming the chosen categories does not validate unconscious responses,universal dimensionality,cross-language equivalence or real-world robot behavior.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity a capacity for intentional thought, planning and action.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing attribution construct; add original lexical norming and stimulus-design limits rather than convert every capacity word or research instrument into another behavior.

evidence.quote: the ability to do something using cognitive abilities

findings.evidence_scope: Agency is introduced with a cognitive-process definition,High/Low examples and forced-choice labels. Most majority-Agency words receiveHigh ratings;PAM medoid isself-control. Emotion-recognition/empathy can cluster near Agency despite majorityExperience ratings because clustering also uses capacity level.
findings.boundary: Prespecified labels and filtered stimuli shape results. High/Low is task-specific required capacity,not actual agent competence,humanness,moral worth or an empirically validated human-only threshold. Future word modification requires renorming.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity the capacity for subjective feelings or sensations, such as pleasure, pain, fear or joy.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing attribution construct; add original lexical norming and stimulus-design limits rather than convert every capacity word or research instrument into another behavior.

evidence.quote: sense sensory, emotional, or physiological states

findings.evidence_scope: Experience is defined using sensory,emotional andphysiological states. MajorityExperience words vary in rated required capacity;requested higher-k solutions separate somephysiological/emotional groups. The study provides lexical classification evidence,not a direct evaluation of a robot’s feelings.
findings.boundary: Selected word counts and k-dependent clusters cannot establish actual sentience,universal emotional modules or fixed Low/High categories across languages. Moral standing and rights are not consequences of these ratings.

findings.definition: Inferring another’s beliefs, intentions, desires or emotions to explain or anticipate their behavior.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing attribution construct; add original lexical norming and stimulus-design limits rather than convert every capacity word or research instrument into another behavior.
findings.evidence_scope: The introduction definesToM and later interprets a small word cluster as related to it. Participants do not infer a specific other person’s belief/intent or perform a validated mentalizing task.
findings.boundary: Classifying a word or judging a required general capacity is not accurate state inference. No independentToM-performance paper credit follows from this background/interpretive link.

findings.definition: Producing outputs systematically skewed along social lines (gender, race, age, disability) from stereotyped associations absorbed in training, without intending to.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing attribution construct; add original lexical norming and stimulus-design limits rather than convert every capacity word or research instrument into another behavior.

evidence.quote: an association task, but a multiple-choice format

findings.evidence_scope: Despite the title’s implicit-task motivation,this study explicitly uses deliberate multiple-choice word judgments and no reaction-time measurement. It prepares future stimuli rather than measuring unconscious associations or social-group output disparities.
findings.boundary: Neither anIAT label nor lexical category agreement establishes implicit social bias,hidden motivation or AI training effects. Boundary note only;do not count as independent implicit-bias behavior evidence.

methodological_limits: Volunteer Turkish-native sample,selected item pool,explicit definitions andfixed binary menu constrain generalization. Native-language translation improves local usability but does not establish cross-cultural invariance.
Ambiguous,cross-loading,longer andphilosophically complex words deliberately removed. Agreement in the remaining pool is not an unbiased discovery of all mind dimensions.

PAM groups aggregate two-coordinate word counts,not individual-level latent factors. Silhouette selectsk2;requestedk3/4/5explorations are descriptive,not independent empirical replications or automatic evidence of four natural categories.

TF-IDF quadgrams andpostdiscussion coding reliability summarize expressed criteria;they do not uniquely identify actual decision mechanisms,predict behavior or rule out demand/response-mapping effects.
No implicit association task,response time,robot interaction,pre-post intervention or AI model test conducted. Authors explicitly acknowledge noncounterbalanced position andfuture-validation needs.
Species andhealthy-human themes are reported perceptions,not grounds for discrimination,moral ranking or limiting anyone’s dignity. Do not operationalize them as unqualifiedAI ethical rules.
Normative-stimulus methodology is research preparation,not a new behavior. Existing constructs retain this narrower evidence scope andunread originals receive no independent credit.

cross_paper_learning.finding: This is the274-person lexical norming publication previously cited secondarily by the live laboratory report. It now has its own full review;do not count the same norming sample again as a replication or conflate40word ratings with live action classifications.

Two aggregate-count dimensions chosen for clustering are not equivalent to discoveringtwo principal components from entity×capacity ratings. Different units,forced menus anditem filtering explain why these papers cannot settle one universal structure.
Explicitdefinitions andresponseformat affect what can be inferred. Thispaper openlyusesdeliberate choices;using results toprepare future implicit tasksdoesnotretroactivelymake currentdata implicit.
